transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
What made me come in is that when I start eating like that, it feels like I can’t stop. It’s like something switches, and even while I’m thinking, “Dennis, just stop already,” I keep going.
During those times when you feel like you can’t stop, do you eat an unusually large amount of food?

Yeah. Like after a project deadline, or if there’s leftover pizza in the apartment, I can eat a whole small pizza, then chips and cereal in my room. It’s way more than I meant to eat—more than my roommates would eat for a normal dinner.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t make myself throw up afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to undo the calories, like using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?
I’m not really sure what counts. I don’t think I do anything specific afterward—I mostly just feel bad about it.
After you have one of these eating episodes, do you intentionally skip meals or go without eating for a while to make up for it?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think about it as trying to make up for it—I just kind of eat normally after, I guess.
When these eating episodes happen, does it feel like you lose control over your eating?
Yeah. Once I start, it’s like I hit a switch and I just keep going, even though part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already.
During these eating episodes, do you eat more quickly than you normally do?
Yeah, I do. I’ll be standing at my desk between homework and a game, and I’m just eating really fast, barely tasting it. Then a few minutes later I realize it’s all gone.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to get rid of the calories?
No, I don’t think so. I just… don’t really do anything afterward to get rid of it.
Do these eating episodes upset you a lot afterward?
Yeah. I feel embarrassed afterward, and kind of grossed out with myself. I’m usually pretty disciplined with school and robotics, so it makes me feel like I’m not in control.
Is your body shape or weight one of the main things that determines how you feel about yourself?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my weight or body shape being a main thing in how I feel about myself.
During these episodes, do you eat even when you’re not physically hungry?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m physically hungry at those times.
After these episodes, do you ever exercise hard specifically to burn off what you ate?
I’m not sure—I haven’t really thought about exercising afterward specifically because of what I ate.
During these episodes, do you usually eat alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you’re eating?
Yeah, usually. If my roommates are around, I’ll eat a normal amount in the kitchen, then take more food back to my room later because I don’t want them to see how much I’m actually eating.
How often do these episodes happen?

Since early in the semester, it’s been most weeks—usually one night a week, sometimes two if I’ve got deadlines or there’s a lot of food in the apartment. It’s been pretty steady like that for the last three or four months.
Do these binge-eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?
Yeah. Afterward I feel embarrassed and kind of grossed out with myself. I’m usually pretty disciplined with school and robotics, so it makes me feel like I’m not really in control.
After you binge, do you ever take laxatives or diuretics to try to offset what you ate?
No, I haven’t taken anything like that.
After one of these episodes, do you feel guilty?
Yeah, I do. I feel embarrassed afterward and pretty disgusted with myself. It feels like I should have more control than that.
